chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) led us in the Zuhr and Asr prayers at the time of the sun's decline, with one adhan and two iqamas, and said: 'I am occupied with a matter, so perform optional prayers.'

key_terms.أَذَانٌ: Adhan — the call to prayer; one adhan for both combined prayers indicates their union
key_terms.إِقَامَتَيْنِ: Two iqamas — despite one adhan, each prayer has its own iqama, confirming they are two distinct prayers being combined
key_terms.تَنَفَّلُوا: Perform nafilah (optional prayers) — the supererogatory prayers normally performed between Zuhr and Asr
key_terms.زَالَتِ الشَّمْسُ: The sun's decline (zawal) — the moment the sun passes its zenith, marking the entry of Zuhr prayer time

ai.seo_question: Did Imam al-Sadiq combine Zuhr and Asr prayers at the start of their time with one adhan and two iqamas?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) combined the Zuhr and Asr prayers at the beginning of their shared time window (upon the sun's decline), using a single adhan with two separate iqamas. After leading the congregation, he excused himself from additional prayers, instructing those present to perform supererogatory (nafilah) prayers on their own. This hadith serves as a primary proof for the permissibility of combining the two midday prayers without a specific journey or hardship excuse, a distinctive position in Shia jurisprudence.
